name: execute_command
description: Run a shell command. Destructive, network, and privilege-escalation commands are blocked. Truncated output reports shown/total counts; narrow or page instead of rerunning variants. Failures report the exit code.
first_use_guidance:
Guidance for later execute_command calls in this turn:
- `sleep` is expensive: it blocks the whole turn on dead time — do not use it unless truly necessary (e.g. waiting for a server to accept connections). Prefer non-blocking patterns: background long-running work (`&` + log file) and poll readiness, or `task_wait` for subagent tasks.

command.description: Shell command. Background long-running servers and redirect their output before probing; never run one in the foreground. Do not pipe interactive commands through `head`, `tail`, `grep`, or `tee`; they can wait for process exit and stall.

pty.description: Use true for interactive CLIs (prompts, QR codes, full-screen UI), false otherwise. Keyboard input is not forwarded. Blocking interactive commands stop after about 10-20 seconds of silence and return partial output; prefer non-blocking or headless flags.
